cd /testbed && git --no-pager status --short && printf '%s\n' '{"title":"Title 1","media:content":{"media:credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}}' | ./jq '{title, credits: .["media:content"].["media:credits"]}'; cd /testbed && rg -n 'Term|INDEX|Index|gen_index|yyerror' src/parser.y && ls tests && rg -n 'Object Identifier|Object Index|\.\["foo"\]' docs

cd /testbed && git --no-pager diff --stat && git --no-pager diff -- src/parser.c | head -140 && sed -n '1,180p' src/parser.y && sed -n '590,820p' src/parser.y && ls tests && grep -nE 'Object Identifier|Object Index|\.\["foo"\]' docs/content/manual*/* && file jq .libs/jq && grep -nE '^(CC|CFLAGS|LDFLAGS) ?=' Makefile && command -v clang && command -v peeky

cd /testbed && git --no-pager log -4 --oneline && git show HEAD:src/parser.y | sed -n '685,745p' && sed -n '340,475p' docs/content/manual/manual.yml && sed -n '1,170p' tests/jq.test && sed -n '1,130p' tests/jqtest && file jq && grep -nE '^(CC|CFLAGS|LDFLAGS) ?=' Makefile && command -v peeky

cd /testbed && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/parser.y')
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('%type <blk> Exp Term\n', '%type <blk> Exp Term TermIndex\n', 1)

old = '''Term '.' '[' Exp ']' '?' {
  $$ = gen_index_opt($1, $4);
} |
Term '.' '[' Exp ']' %prec NONOPT {
  $$ = gen_index($1, $4);
} |
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, '')
s = s.replace("Term '['", "TermIndex '['")
anchor = '\nArgs:\n'
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
s = s.replace(anchor, '''
TermIndex:
Term {
  $$ = $1;
} |
Term '.' {
  $$ = $1;
}

Args:
''')
p.write_text(s)
p = Path('tests/jq.test')

anchor = '."foo"."bar"\n'
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
s = s.replace(anchor, '''# Generic indexes can be chained with or without a dot.

[4,null]

{"foo":[1,2,3]}

p.write_text(s)
p = Path('docs/content/manual/manual.yml')
s = p.read_text()
anchor = '''          only for identifier-like strings).

      - title: "Array Index: `.[<number>]`"
'''
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
s = s.replace(anchor, '''          only for identifier-like strings).

          Indexes can be chained, as in `.foo["bar"]` or
          `.foo.["bar"]`, which both mean `.foo | .["bar"]`.
          The optional dot before brackets also works with array indexes,

        examples:
          - program: '.["media:content"].["media:credits"]'
            input: '{"media:content": {"media:credits": "Credits"}}'

      - title: "Array Index: `.[<number>]`"
''')
p.write_text(s)
